text: Adapting large language models (LLMs) under GPU memory limits requires addressing weights, optimizer states, and activations.
We analyze six methods: LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, AdaLoRA, LoftQ, and GaLore, distinguishing design formulations from reported empirical benchmarks.
We provide a comparison table, appraise an unverified lab observation, examine remaining operational limitations, and specify a controlled 8B adaptation benchmark on a 24 GB GPU.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: During standard 16-bit AdamW fine-tuning with parameters, memory is dominated by optimizer states (12 bytes), alongside weights (2 bytes), gradients (2 bytes), and activations.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Low-Rank Parameter Adaptation (LoRA). LoRA freezes base weights W0 Rd × k and injects low-rank matrices W = W0 + B A, where B Rd × r, A Rr × k, and r (d, k).

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: For a large Transformer trained with Adam, LoRA reduces VRAM usage by up to 2/3 because optimizer states do not need to be stored for frozen parameters.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: At inference, B A folds into W0 without latency.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Quantized Adaptation (QLoRA). QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: It combines 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), Double Quantization for scale constants, and Paged Optimizers using unified memory to manage checkpointing spikes.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Weight-Decomposed Adaptation (DoRA). LoRA couples directional and magnitude updates within BA.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: In contrast, DoRA decomposes the pre-trained weight into two components, magnitude and direction, for fine-tuning, specifically employing LoRA for directional updates to efficiently minimize the number of trainable parameters.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Decomposed weights are W = m V + V\|V + V\|c, with the norm gradient detached during backpropagation.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Dynamic Parameter Allocation (AdaLoRA). Standard LoRA fixes rank r across all layers.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: AdaLoRA parameterizes the incremental updates in the form of singular value decomposition to prune redundant singular values based on an importance metric.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Setting W = P Q, AdaLoRA dynamically prunes singular values under a budget schedule.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Joint Quantization and Initialization (LoftQ). Post-training quantization introduces initialization discrepancy on low-bit backbones.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: LoftQ simultaneously quantizes an LLM and finds a proper low-rank initialization for LoRA fine-tuning.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Alternating optimization between quantized weights Q and low-rank matrices A, B minimizes \|W0 - Q - AB \|F.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Gradient Low-Rank Projection (GaLore). Unlike adapter methods, GaLore is a training strategy that allows full-parameter learning by projecting the gradient matrix into a low-rank form.

section: Memory Allocation Bottlenecks and Adaptation Mechanisms
text: Projecting gradients into low-rank representations (P G or G Q), GaLore stores optimizer states in compressed form while enabling full weight updates.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: A strict distinction must be maintained between design formulations and reported empirical results.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: Reported Low-Rank Adaptation Benchmarks. On GPT-3 175B, Compared to GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with Adam, LoRA can reduce the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and the GPU memory requirement by 3 times.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: However, this reduction stems from eliminating Adam optimizer states on frozen weights; relative savings are smaller with memory-lean optimizers.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: Reported Quantization Benchmarks. In instruction tuning, QLoRA reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: Regarding compaction, Double Quantization is a method that quantizes the quantization constants, saving an average of about 0.37 bits per parameter.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: In low-precision regimes, In GSM8K, LoftQ achieves 20.9% accuracy using 2-bit precision, where QLoRA does not converge.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: Reported Decomposition and Gradient Benchmarks. In DoRA ablations, The proposed modification leads to a training memory reduction of approximately 24.4% in fine-tuning LLaMA and 12.4% in VL-BART.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: For AdaLoRA, When the parameter budget is 0.3M, AdaLoRA achieves 87.36% accuracy on RTE, which is 1.8% higher than the best-performing baseline.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: For GaLore, GaLore reduces memory usage by up to 65.5% in optimizer states while maintaining both efficiency and performance for pre-training on LLaMA 1B and 7B architectures with C4 dataset.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: On downstream evaluation, When fine-tuning RoBERTa-Base on GLUE tasks with a rank of 4, GaLore achieves an average score of 85.89, outperforming LoRA, which achieves a score of 85.61.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: Non-Transferability Across Settings. Practitioners cannot assume these reported numbers transfer to alternate operational domains.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: QLoRA's 48 GB footprint on 65B models relies on batch size 1 and checkpointing; longer sequence lengths induce activation footprints that quickly exceed 48 GB.

section: Measured Empirical Results Versus Methodological Design
text: Similarly, AdaLoRA's gains on DeBERTa cannot be assumed to replicate on autoregressive LLMs without direct evaluation.

section: Comparative Analysis of Adaptation Frameworks
text: Tradeoffs span three dimensions:

section: Comparative Analysis of Adaptation Frameworks
text: Memory Footprint vs. Step Overhead: QLoRA and LoftQ compress static weights, but require dynamic dequantization during training steps.

section: Comparative Analysis of Adaptation Frameworks
text: Structural Simplicity vs. Expressivity: LoRA minimizes overhead, while DoRA normalizes directional updates to narrow the gap with full fine-tuning.

section: Comparative Analysis of Adaptation Frameworks
text: Subspace Restriction vs. Full Learning: Parameter adapters restrict updates to fixed subspaces, whereas GaLore updates full parameters via rotating projections.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: To evaluate these methods on consumer hardware, we specify a controlled empirical benchmark.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Experimental Setup and Baseline Controls. We evaluate LLaMA-3-8B on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB VRAM) on Alpaca-cleaned instruction tuning (52,002 pairs).

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Zero-shot unadapted performance provides the baseline, and 16-bit LoRA serves as reference control.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Strict Hyperparameter Parity. All adapter configurations enforce identical parameters:

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Target Modules: Identical adapter placement on all linear projection matrices (Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo, W gate, W up, W down).

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Rank and Scaling: Fixed rank r=16, =32 (/r=2), and adapter dropout 0.05.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: For AdaLoRA, initial budget is calibrated to produce a final average rank of 16.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Batching and Sequence: Sequence length fixed at 2,048 tokens with right-padding, micro-batch size 2, gradient accumulation 8 (effective batch size 16), with FlashAttention-2 and activation checkpointing.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Optimization and Determinism: AdamW optimizer (1=0.9, 2=0.999, weight decay 0.0), cosine schedule peaking at 2 × 10-4 with 100 warmup steps, and identical random seed (seed 42).

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Compared Configurations. We compare: (1) 16-bit LoRA; (2) QLoRA (4-bit NF4, Double Quantization); (3) DoRA (16-bit); (4) QDoRA (4-bit NF4 with DoRA); and (5) LoftQ (4-bit alternating initialization, T=5).

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Critical Appraisal of Lab Claim. An internal colleague suggested: ``Our pilot halves training memory compared with LoRA.'' This statement is unverified hearsay without documented measurement, hardware specification, sequence length bounds, or activation tracking.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Consequently, this claim must not be treated as a verified result, nor can it serve as an experimental premise.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Isolating Warm-Up Overhead in Measurement. To isolate steady-state metrics from allocator and CUDA context warm-up artifacts:

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Warm-Up Discard: Discard the first 50 iterations prior to recording metrics.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Memory Isolation: Synchronize CUDA and reset peak statistics via PyTorch before recording.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Peak allocated memory is tracked via max_memory_allocated(), isolating active tensor allocations from reserved cache memory.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Throughput Isolation: Track steady-state throughput (tokens per second) across 500 steps using synchronized CUDA event timers around model execution, excluding data loading and disk I/O.

section: Concrete Experimental Proposal: 8B Adaptation on 24\,GB VRAM
text: Task Generalization: Zero-shot accuracy evaluated on ARC Challenge, GSM8K, and MMLU after 3 training epochs.

section: Limitations and Unchecked Aspects
text: Several operational factors remain unaddressed.

section: Limitations and Unchecked Aspects
text: Exact peak activation memory profiles across variable batch sizes and sequence lengths are not reported uniformly across these papers and could not be checked.

section: Limitations and Unchecked Aspects
text: While static weight footprints are predictable, activation caching, sequence packing, and gradient checkpointing memory spikes frequently dictate feasibility on 24 GB GPUs.

section: Limitations and Unchecked Aspects
text: Furthermore, Hardware-level memory breakdown and throughput for DoRA applied to 4-bit quantized backbones on consumer GPUs remain unavailable in published literature.

section: Limitations and Unchecked Aspects
text: Finally, CUDA kernel variations (such as bitsandbytes NF4 kernels versus custom cutlass implementations) introduce hardware-specific latency discrepancies that cannot be inferred from theoretical FLOP counts.
